BCM2_05_AWX_7240_01_Sec_Definition.title: Definition – Function, Systematics, and Meta-Embedding of the Awareness Function
BCM2_05_AWX_7240_01_Sec_Definition.description: Defines Awareness as a dynamic, systemically differentiated condition for converting potential benefit into effective benefit. Awareness integrates visceral, emotional, and cognitive processes and determines whether behavior becomes benefit-effective at the moment of decision (= Moment of Truth). The definition follows the meta-axiomatics MA_0.00 l–r and z–zc.

core_definition.statement: Awareness is the necessary condition for converting a potential benefit (individual, collective, identity-based) into effective benefit at the Moment of Truth.
core_definition.extended: Awareness means consciousness of one’s own impact—positive or negative—on individual, collective, and identity-based benefit types. It spans physiological (SYS 0), affective-emotional (SYS 1), and cognitive-reflective (SYS 2) system levels.
core_definition.formal_condition: U_eff,X(t*) = U_pot,X(t*) × A_SYSi,X(t*), X ∈ {INU, KNU, IDN}, i ∈ {0,1,2}

SYS0_Instant.definition: Automatic visceral activation – instant awareness without conscious processing.
SYS0_Instant.formal: A_SYS0 = 1 under immediate sensory or affective reaction

SYS1_Affective.definition: Emotional awareness of the meaning and social resonance of one’s behavior.

SYS2_Reflective.definition: Cognitive awareness of impact, consequences, and meaning in the context of rules and norms.

exception_rule.Instant_INU: Physiologically felt individual benefit effects (e.g., pain, hunger, dopamine kick) do not require conscious awareness – SYS 0 activates automatically.
exception_rule.Instant_IDN: Emotional-social, instantly felt identity effects (e.g., applause, exclusion) are activated without reflection.
exception_rule.Instant_KNU: Collective benefit can only have instant impact via mediation (through IDN or empathy); direct instant collective awareness does not exist.

meta_interpretation.MA_0.00l: Defines Awareness as the necessary transformation condition between U_pot and U_eff.
meta_interpretation.MA_0.00m: Defines the 0–1 continuum of Awareness: 0 = no awareness (habit), 1 = fully conscious transformation.
meta_interpretation.MA_0.00n: Anchors Awareness as a process across system levels 0–2 (Instant → Affect → Reflection).
meta_interpretation.MA_0.00o: Binds Awareness to visceral baseline reactions (System 0 per Loewenstein).
meta_interpretation.MA_0.00p: Defines dynamic interaction between systems 0–2 as a meta-feedback process.
meta_interpretation.MA_0.00q: Enables cultural and neuroeconomic modulation of awareness thresholds.
meta_interpretation.MA_0.00r: Integrates compliance and honesty as meta-awareness effects (System 2).

meta_feedback.description: Awareness learns via feedback from behavioral consequences and corrects its own impact estimation (MA 0.00zc).

meta_constraints.C1: Awareness is always situational (Moment of Truth must be defined).
meta_constraints.C2: Awareness cannot be maximal simultaneously in SYS0 and SYS2 (hyper-dissonance).
meta_constraints.C3: Awareness ends when habitualization > θ_habit or total_uncertainty > θ_uncertainty.

governance.validation_rule: Σ|ΔA_SYSi| ≤ θ_meta ∧ C1–C3 satisfied → Definition = STABLE

BCM2_05_AWX_7240_01_Sec_Definition.author: FehrAdvice BCM Kernel – Meta Integration Team

BCM2_05_AWX_7240_02_Sec_Scope_Context.title: Scope & Context – Reach, situational conditions, and systemic linkage of the Awareness function
BCM2_05_AWX_7240_02_Sec_Scope_Context.description: Describes the functional reach of Awareness across benefit types, contexts, and decision situations. Awareness (A_SYS0–2) acts exclusively situationally at the Moment of Truth and mediates between potential and effective benefit. This definition follows meta-axioms MA_0.00 l–n, p–r and z–zc.

functional_scope.rule: Awareness only acts when at least one benefit type is active at the Moment of Truth.
functional_scope.formal: A_total(t*) = f(A_INU, A_KNU, A_IDN) | A_X(t) = 0 for all t ≠ t*

context_integration.definition: Awareness is fully context-dependent. It emerges when stimuli, norms, emotions, or institutional signals are in a recognizable relationship with individual, collective, or identity-based benefit.

moment_of_truth.definition: The Moment of Truth (t*) is the decision point at which potential benefit can be transformed into behavior via Awareness.
moment_of_truth.formal: A_SYSi(t*) > 0 ⇔ decision active ∧ context salience > θ_awareness
moment_of_truth.implication: Awareness can act only at moment t*, not before or after; this distinguishes it from knowledge or attitudes.

meta_scope_differentiation.SYS0: Instant Awareness – reflexive visceral activation, no conscious reflection.
meta_scope_differentiation.SYS1: Affective Awareness – emotional resonance, coupled to social signals.
meta_scope_differentiation.SYS2: Reflective Awareness – cognitive-reflective integration and evaluation of consequences.
meta_scope_differentiation.transition_rule: A_SYSi(t*) can dynamically shift across system levels (e.g., SYS0 → SYS1 → SYS2) per MA_0.00p.

contextual_determinants.meta_condition: All determinants must be ≤ θ_capacity and ≥ θ_salience for A_SYSi(t*) > 0.

meta_constraints.C1: Awareness is valid only if relevant context (C_rel) exists.
meta_constraints.C2: Awareness must not be maximal simultaneously in SYS0 and SYS2.
meta_constraints.C3: Collective benefit (KNU) is always awareness-required; instant KNU is not possible.
meta_constraints.C4: Awareness decreases when complexity or uncertainty thresholds are exceeded.

governance.validation_rule: Σ|ΔA_SYSi| ≤ θ_meta ∧ C1–C4 satisfied → Scope = VALID

BCM2_05_AWX_7240_02_Sec_Scope_Context.author: FehrAdvice BCM Kernel – Meta Integration Team

BCM2_05_AWX_7240_03_Sec_Objectives.title: Objectives – Purpose, function, and direction of effect of the Awareness function
BCM2_05_AWX_7240_03_Sec_Objectives.description: Defines the functional objectives of the Awareness function (A_SYS0–2) within BCM. Awareness acts as a necessary transformer that converts potential benefit into effective benefit and enables behavior at the Moment of Truth. Objectives follow MA_0.00 l–r and MA_0.00 z–zc.

O1.title: Transformation from potential to effective benefit
O1.definition: Awareness enables U_pot → U_eff by making benefit salient and action-effective.

O2.title: Reducing the knowledge–action gap
O2.definition: Awareness closes the gap between cognitive knowledge (SYS2) and actual behavior (SYS0–1).

O3.title: Integration of external effects
O3.definition: Awareness includes consciousness of positive and negative impacts on other people or groups.

O4.title: Systemic differentiation
O4.definition: Awareness integrates three system levels (visceral, affective, reflective) into a dynamic unity.

O5.title: Enabling compliance and honesty
O5.definition: Awareness enables reflective self-evaluation regarding rule compliance and ethical integrity.

O6.title: Maintaining meta-coherence
O6.definition: Awareness functions as a control variable ensuring benefit types, willingness, and context remain consistent.

O7.title: Feedback-based learning capability
O7.definition: Awareness adapts via feedback loops to observed action outcomes.

O8.title: Strengthening collective decision quality
O8.definition: Shared awareness makes collective decisions more coherent, transparent, and fair.

systemic_function.definition: Awareness acts as a multiplicative amplifier and filter between benefit modules (7234–7236) and Willingness (7243).

evaluation_metrics.meta_validation: 9477_STAT validates all metrics in conjunction with 9251_WATCHDOG

governance.validation_rule: If O1–O8 are functionally satisfied and Σ|ΔA_SYSi| ≤ θ_meta → Objectives = VALID

BCM2_05_AWX_7240_03_Sec_Objectives.author: FehrAdvice BCM Kernel – Meta Integration Team

obj_core.statement: Potential benefit becomes effective only if Awareness > 0 at moment t*.
obj_core.interpretation: Awareness acts as multiplier and filter between benefit potential and behavior.

axioms.title: Community relevance
axioms.definition: Awareness is the consciousness that one’s behavior affects the benefit of a relevant community.

axioms.title: Social externalities
axioms.definition: Awareness becomes behavior-effective only when effects on collective or identity-based benefit of a relevant community are recognized.

axioms.title: Time-delayed individual benefit
axioms.definition: Awareness also includes individual benefit with delayed effects that must be made salient anticipatorily.
axioms.formula: A_mod(t) > 0 ⇒ N_ind(t+h) salient if h > θ_instant

axioms.title: Moment of Truth
axioms.definition: Awareness acts exclusively at the moment of decision.

sub_axioms.title: General awareness as a learning effect
sub_axioms.definition: General awareness emerges only through repeated situational activation.

sub_axioms.name: Dynamic salience
sub_axioms.definition: Awareness changes depending on the temporal dynamics of the perceived context.
formula: P(A_i = 1 | C_i, t, S_i) = χ(C_i, σ_dyn(C_i,t), S_i)
sub_axioms.notes: Extension validated and released – part of the productive Awareness function.

axioms.title: Positive and negative impact
axioms.definition: Awareness necessarily includes both positive and negative impacts of behavior.

axioms.title: Instant-benefit exceptions
axioms.definition: Certain benefit effects occur instantly without awareness (INU_instant, IDN_instant). Collective benefit is never instant.
axioms.formula: If X ∈ {INU_instant, IDN_instant} → A_X(t*) = 1; if X = KNU → awareness-required

axioms.title: General vs. situational
axioms.definition: Only situational impact-awareness at the Moment of Truth is behavior-effective.
axioms.formula: A_general ≠ A_situational; only A_situational(t*) is relevant

axioms.title: Inter-individual differences
axioms.definition: Awareness levels vary between individuals due to cognitive, emotional, social, and biological factors.

sub_axioms.title: Cognitive structuring capability
sub_axioms.definition: Whether awareness becomes reflective depends on literacy, media competence, and logical model-building.

axioms.title: Context dependence
axioms.definition: Awareness is fully context-bound.

sub_axioms.title: Context as amplifier or blocker
sub_axioms.definition: Context factors can amplify or block awareness.

axioms.title: Limitation
axioms.definition: Awareness is limited by attentional capacity.

sub_axioms.title: Uncertainty and ambiguity
sub_axioms.definition: Ambiguity, risk, and uncertainty slow or distort awareness learning.

axioms.title: Salience and priming
axioms.definition: Awareness emerges only if benefit is salient or activated via priming.

sub_axioms.title: Hyper-awareness
sub_axioms.definition: Awareness can be exaggerated such that even minimally relevant benefits become salient.
sub_axioms.formula: A_mod(t) ≫ A_norm(t) ⇒ ∀N_x(t) salient, even if Relevance(N_x) ≈ 0

sub_axioms.title: Awareness blockade
sub_axioms.definition: Awareness can be blocked such that relevant benefits do not become salient.
sub_axioms.formula: A_mod(t) = 0 ⇒ N_x(t) not salient although Relevance(N_x) > 0

axioms.title: Habitualization
axioms.definition: Habitual behavioral patterns require no awareness.

sub_axioms.title: Decay effect
sub_axioms.definition: As habitualization increases, functional access to awareness decreases.

sub_axioms.title: Clinical relevance
sub_axioms.definition: Persistent deviations (hyper or blockade) become clinically relevant when distress or functional loss emerges.

axioms.title: Cognitive attention span
axioms.definition: Awareness increases with available attention and decreases under overload.

axioms.title: Cognitive load
axioms.definition: Awareness decreases with increasing cognitive burden from parallel tasks or information.

axioms.title: Evidence availability
axioms.definition: Awareness increases with clarity, simplicity, and visibility of evidence for impact.

axioms.title: Availability heuristic
axioms.definition: Awareness increases with the mental availability of examples or memories.

axioms.title: Emotional valence
axioms.definition: Positive or negative affect increases awareness for the associated benefit.

axioms.title: Fear as amplifier
axioms.definition: Fear increases awareness for negative impact particularly strongly.

axioms.title: Hope as amplifier
axioms.definition: Hope increases awareness for positive impact.

axioms.title: Affective resonance
axioms.definition: Awareness increases when behavior is linked to strong emotional reactions.

axioms.title: Social norm pressure
axioms.definition: Awareness increases when behavior is strongly socially sanctioned or rewarded.

axioms.title: Social mirroring
axioms.definition: Awareness increases when behavior is visibly mirrored by peers or relevant others.

axioms.title: Network effects
axioms.definition: Awareness increases when behavior is amplified in social networks.

axioms.title: Institutional legitimacy
axioms.definition: Awareness increases when behavior is supported by institutions perceived as legitimate.

axioms.title: Institutional trust
axioms.definition: Lack of trust in institutions reduces awareness levels.

axioms.title: Rule clarity
axioms.definition: The clearer the rules, the higher awareness of their impact.

axioms.title: Cultural narratives
axioms.definition: Awareness increases when behavior is embedded in existing narratives.

axioms.title: Symbols and rituals
axioms.definition: Cultural symbols and rituals increase awareness particularly strongly.

axioms.title: Priming effects
axioms.definition: Conscious or unconscious priming increases the probability that benefit becomes salient.

axioms.title: Biological factors
axioms.definition: Awareness varies with biological properties such as age, sex, neurodiversity.

axioms.title: Energetic state
axioms.definition: Awareness decreases with exhaustion and increases with high energy.

axioms.title: Interactive determinants
axioms.definition: Awareness results from interaction of multiple determinants (e.g., Emotion × Norm_pressure).

axioms.title: Awareness INU
axioms.definition: Awareness for individual benefit means consciousness that one’s behavior has positive or negative impact on one’s own individual benefit.

axioms.title: Awareness KNU
axioms.definition: Awareness for collective benefit means consciousness that one’s behavior has positive or negative impact on the benefit of a community or group.

axioms.title: Awareness IDN
axioms.definition: Awareness for identity-based benefit means consciousness that one’s behavior has positive or negative impact on belonging, recognition, or identity.

axioms.title: Differentiation by benefit type
axioms.definition: Awareness differs by benefit type: INU strongest, KNU weakest, IDN strongly context-dependent.

axioms.title: Instant INU
axioms.definition: Physiologically felt individual benefit effects (e.g., hunger, pain, fatigue, dopamine kick) are instant and require no awareness.

axioms.title: Instant IDN
axioms.definition: Social-emotional identity effects (e.g., applause, shame, symbols) are instant and require no awareness.

axioms.title: No instant KNU
axioms.definition: Collective benefit is never instant. All KNU effects are awareness-required.
axioms.formula: For all U_pot,KNU: A_KNU(t*) < 1 without awareness

axioms.title: Interaction INU ↔ KNU
axioms.definition: Awareness for KNU increases when an INU is simultaneously affected.

axioms.title: Interaction INU ↔ IDN
axioms.definition: Awareness for INU increases when the behavior is simultaneously identity-relevant.

axioms.title: Interaction KNU ↔ IDN
axioms.definition: Awareness for KNU increases when belonging to a community is strongly identity-salient.

axioms.title: Awareness hierarchy
axioms.definition: In conflict cases, INU awareness dominates IDN, and IDN dominates KNU.

axioms.title: Awareness overlay
axioms.definition: Awareness for one benefit type can temporarily override awareness for another.

axioms.title: Awareness multiplication
axioms.definition: Total effective benefit is the sum of awareness-filtered benefit types.

axioms.title: Awareness sensitivity
axioms.definition: Awareness threshold differs by benefit type: INU low threshold, KNU high threshold.

axioms.title: Awareness amplification via multi-effect
axioms.definition: If behavior affects INU, KNU, and IDN simultaneously, awareness increases multiplicatively.

axioms.title: Complexity reduction
axioms.definition: Awareness decreases as decision complexity increases.

axioms.title: Necessity of framing
axioms.definition: Under high complexity, awareness becomes possible only via simplification, framing, or heuristics.

axioms.title: Failure Awareness Gap
axioms.definition: Awareness is systematically distorted when failures remain communicatively, institutionally, or culturally invisible. The Failure Awareness Gap describes the collective perception gap that arises when errors are socially stigmatized, not reported, or algorithmically filtered out. It grows under high power distance, low transparency standards, and low psychological safety.
axioms.interpretation: If ΔAwareness_F rises above 0.25, the system loses adaptive perceptual capability (perceptual lock-in). The axiom binds communicative and cultural determinants to the awareness function and explains why systems recognize failures too late.
empirical_reference: Eskreis-Winkler et al. (2025) – The Failure Gap
axioms.author: FehrAdvice BEATRIX Kernel Integration Team

axioms.title: Environmental uncertainty
axioms.definition: If consequences of behavior in the environment are uncertain, awareness decreases.

axioms.title: Interpersonal uncertainty
axioms.definition: Awareness decreases when it is unclear how other individuals will react.

axioms.title: Institutional uncertainty
axioms.definition: If trust in institutions is lacking or rules are unclear, awareness decreases.

axioms.title: Epistemic uncertainty
axioms.definition: If knowledge about cause–effect relationships is missing, awareness drops to zero.

axioms.title: Uncertainty accumulation
axioms.definition: Awareness decreases more strongly when multiple uncertainty types occur simultaneously.

axioms.title: Uncertainty differentiation
axioms.definition: Awareness reacts with different strengths to uncertainty types: epistemic > institutional > interpersonal > environmental.

axioms.title: Complexity–uncertainty interaction
axioms.definition: Complexity amplifies the effect of uncertainty and reduces awareness disproportionately.

axioms.title: Need for institutional aids
axioms.definition: Under high complexity and uncertainty, awareness can be secured only via institutional orientation aids (e.g., rules, standards, labels).
axioms.formula: If Complexity & Uncertainty high → A_X(t*) = f(Institutional_aids)

axioms.title: Situationality
axioms.definition: Awareness exists only in specific situations and contexts. It is not permanent.

axioms.title: Fluctuation
axioms.definition: Awareness levels fluctuate strongly over time depending on context and person factors.

axioms.title: Decay effect
axioms.definition: Without renewed triggers, awareness decays exponentially.

axioms.title: Reactivation
axioms.definition: Awareness can be reactivated or strengthened via repeated triggers.

axioms.title: Habitual attenuation
axioms.definition: Repeated exposure can weaken awareness if a stimulus becomes routine.
axioms.formula: A_X(t*) → 0 under high repetition without variation

axioms.title: Life-phase dependence
axioms.definition: Awareness varies systematically across life phases (childhood, youth, adulthood, old age).

axioms.title: Life events
axioms.definition: Certain major events (e.g., birth, death, illness, job loss) change awareness abruptly.

axioms.title: Shock trigger
axioms.definition: Sudden shock events increase awareness massively and immediately.

axioms.title: Long-term stabilization
axioms.definition: Repeated confrontation with stimuli can stabilize awareness long-term if stimuli remain variable and salient.

axioms.title: Journey integration
axioms.definition: Awareness acts as a trigger in specific phases of the Behavioral Change Journey.

axioms.title: Suppression
axioms.definition: Awareness can be consciously or unconsciously suppressed if it is unpleasant or threatening.
axioms.formula: If Awareness → strong negative emotion → A_X(t*) ↓

axioms.title: Cognitive vs. emotional split
axioms.definition: Individuals can be cognitively informed about an impact without emotional awareness emerging.

axioms.title: Norm-conflict blockade
axioms.definition: Awareness can be blocked when different social norms send contradictory behavioral signals.

axioms.title: False awareness
axioms.definition: Misinformation, propaganda, or distorted frames can create awareness that is factually wrong.

axioms.title: Collective overlay
axioms.definition: Collective narratives or group identities can override or suppress individual awareness.

new_axiom.title: Mirror coherence and awareness dissonance
new_axiom.definition: Awareness responds to the difference between self-image (I_t) and social feedback (S_t), measured as Mirror Gap ΔI_t. Small differences promote learning-awareness; large differences activate protective-awareness.
new_axiom.author: FehrAdvice BEATRIX Kernel

axioms.title: Segment dependence
axioms.definition: Awareness levels vary systematically across segments defined in 7257.

axioms.title: Player types
axioms.definition: Awareness levels differ by player type (e.g., cooperative, competitive, strategic) per 9479.

axioms.title: Cultural differentiation
axioms.definition: Awareness varies strongly across cultures due to different narratives, symbols, and institutions.

axioms.title: Education and competence level
axioms.definition: Awareness increases with higher education/competence and decreases with low knowledge.

axioms.title: Socioeconomic status
axioms.definition: Awareness depends on socioeconomic status: resource abundance enables higher awareness.

axioms.title: Aggregation of individual awareness
axioms.definition: Collective awareness level results from aggregating individual awareness values within a group.

axioms.title: Dynamic multiplicity
axioms.definition: Aggregated awareness is non-linear and determined by dynamic weights (e.g., influence of individuals).
axioms.formula: A_Group(t*) = Σ w_i * A_i(t*), w_i ≠ constant

axioms.title: Awareness cascades
axioms.definition: An awareness statement or action can trigger a cascade that increases awareness in others.

axioms.title: Awareness spillover
axioms.definition: Awareness in one domain can strengthen or activate awareness in other domains.

axioms.title: Awareness blockades
axioms.definition: Toxic communication (e.g., hate speech, targeted disinformation) can block awareness at the collective level.

A5_Requirements_v5.0.title: Requirements – input conditions and determinants of the Awareness function
A5_Requirements_v5.0.definition: Defines the structural, contextual, and psychological prerequisites under which Awareness (A_SYS0–2) can become effective at the Moment of Truth. Awareness requires a defined benefit base, an impact mapping between behavior and benefit, and defined determinants at cognitive, emotional, social, institutional, cultural, and communicative levels.

requirements.R1_Benefit_Base: INU, KNU, and IDN must be fully defined and operationalized.
requirements.R2_Impact_Relations: The mapping between behavior and benefit (positive/negative) must be known or observable.
requirements.R4_Time_Context: Awareness is situational; the Moment of Truth (t*) must be contextualized, time-unambiguous, and salience-capable.
requirements.R5_Instant_Exceptions: Special logic: INU_instant and IDN_instant act without awareness; KNU is always awareness-required.
requirements.R6_Segmentation: Awareness varies by segment logic (7257) and player types (9479).
requirements.R7_Communicative_Dynamics: Collective awareness is additionally influenced by communicative distortions (overconfidence, survivorship bias, failure gap). Together they form the Awareness Bias Block.

R8_Thresholds.Awareness_FailureGap: ΔAwareness_F > 0.25 ⇒ perceptual lock-in, automatic watchdog trigger.

inputs: Communication conditions (Failure Gap, Overconfidence, Survivorship Bias)

A5_Requirements_v5.0.validation_rule: All determinants defined ∧ C_rel valid ∧ Σ|ΔA_SYSi| ≤ θ_meta → Awareness applicable
A5_Requirements_v5.0.author: FehrAdvice BEATRIX Kernel Integration Team

A6_Integration_v5.0.title: Integration – systemic linkage of the Awareness function with other BCM modules
A6_Integration_v5.0.definition: Defines the logical, functional, and governance interfaces between the Awareness function (7240) and the other core modules of BCM 2.0. Awareness acts as an intermediate transformation variable between benefit, context, uncertainty, complexity, and willingness. In v5.0, communicative distortions (Bias Block: Overconfidence, Survivorship Bias, Failure Gap) are additionally integrated.

bias_block_coupling.definition: Awareness is coupled to the Bias Block consisting of Overconfidence, Survivorship Bias, and Failure Gap.
formal: Bias_total(t) = Bias_conf + Bias_surv + Bias_fail + κ(Bias_conf × Bias_surv × Bias_fail)

integration_logic.core: Awareness modulates willingness via bias-weighted effectiveness: W_eff = f(U_eff × (1 - Bias_total))
integration_logic.watchdog_rule: If ΔAwareness_F > 0.25 or κ > 0.1 → Event: AWX_FailureGap_Alert
integration_logic.meta_condition: Awareness stable if Bias_total < θ_Bias and Σ|ΔA_SYSi| ≤ θ_meta

governance.validation_rule: All upstream modules available ∧ watchdog active ∧ Σ|ΔA_SYSi| ≤ θ_meta → Integration = VALID

A6_Integration_v5.0.author: FehrAdvice BEATRIX Kernel Integration Team

A7_Boundaries_v5.0.title: Boundaries – delimiting the Awareness function from related concepts and bias influences
A7_Boundaries_v5.0.definition: A7 specifies what Awareness is not within BCM 2.0. With v5.0, boundaries against systemic, communicative, and bias-based pseudo-awareness states are added. Awareness refers exclusively to real-time cognitive, emotional, or reflective processing of one’s own benefit impact at the Moment of Truth—independent of socially mediated frames, discourses, or perceptual distortions.
boundaries: Awareness ≠ knowledge (information can exist without consciousness).
Awareness ≠ attitude (preferential, but not real-time behavior-relevant).
Awareness ≠ motivation (motivation can exist without awareness of impact).
Awareness ≠ automatic processes (exception: instant INU or IDN).
Awareness ≠ norm enforcement (conformity can occur without consciousness).
Awareness ≠ a stable trait (it is dynamic and context-dependent).
Awareness ≠ benefit itself (it mediates benefit but does not create it).
Awareness ≠ full behavioral control (it is necessary but not sufficient).
Awareness ≠ transparency (transparency can exist without being perceived).
Awareness ≠ feedback (feedback creates awareness only if internalized).
Awareness ≠ discourse (social debates do not create individual awareness per se).
Awareness ≠ data awareness (algorithmic display does not replace impact consciousness).
Awareness ≠ false awareness (misinterpretations or framing create pseudo-consciousness).
A7_Boundaries_v5.0.author: FehrAdvice BEATRIX Kernel – Awareness Extension Team

A8_UseCases: Simulation of behavior gaps (knowledge vs. doing)
A9_Limitations: Awareness is a multiplier, not a full explanation

A10_License_and_Governance_v5.0.title: License & Governance – control architecture, ethical use, and bias monitoring
A10_License_and_Governance_v5.0.definition: Regulates usage, control, and governance of the Awareness function within BCM 2.0. In v5.0, automated monitoring of communicative distortions (Overconfidence, Survivorship Bias, Failure Gap) via Watchdog module 9251 is introduced. This checks perceptual integrity of Awareness in real time.

ownership.mandatory_status: Mandatory module – without Awareness no valid simulation or intervention architecture.

usage_rules.R1: Awareness may be used exclusively within licensed BCM models.
usage_rules.R2: All extensions must be axiomatically consistent and meta-validated.
usage_rules.R3: Faulty implementations or uncontrolled bias amplification trigger automatic watchdog checks.
usage_rules.R4: Every application must be disclosed and documented (governance protocol duty).
usage_rules.R5: Covert influence or manipulative use of the Awareness function is excluded.
usage_rules.R6: Goal is to promote fair, transparent, and adaptive decision architectures.

bias_monitoring.description: Automated monitoring of communicative distortions in the Awareness system.
bias_monitoring.formal_rule: Bias_total = Bias_conf + Bias_surv + Bias_fail + κ(Bias_conf × Bias_surv × Bias_fail)
bias_monitoring.meta_integration: Bias monitoring is an integral part of the BCM Watchdog core. It ensures perceptual integrity across all usage levels.

ethics_and_responsibility.E1: Awareness interventions must not cause psychologically or socially harmful effects.
ethics_and_responsibility.E2: All applications must aim to foster perception, not distort it.
ethics_and_responsibility.E3: The module serves to increase collective orientation, fairness, and decision quality.
ethics_and_responsibility.E4: Users and organizations bear full responsibility for integrity, transparency, and traceability of applications.

license_terms.license_scope: Awareness (BCM2_05_AWX), including bias monitoring and Failure Gap.

A10_License_and_Governance_v5.0.author: FehrAdvice BEATRIX Kernel Governance Team
